body.statement: Enumerate all minimal residual hedges of size at most three, optimize or two-approximate that relaxation, and verify the returned \(A\) by alternating restriction of \(G[V\setminus A]\) to directed ancestors of \(s\) and the bidirected component of \(s\). If verification succeeds, an exact relaxation optimum is globally exact and the rounded answer costs at most \(2\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\). If verification fails, deletion-based minimization returns a verifiable \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) with \(|R|>3\).
body.justification: The interface safely exploits low rank without pretending to recognize the promise from a successful run.
body.gap: The WPMAX-SAT and ILP formulations of Elahi and coauthors solve unrestricted MCID but do not return a violated-rank certificate, while explicit bounded-rank hitting-set algorithms assume the promise externally.
body.consumer: RC2 and Gurobi users receive either a certified solution guarantee or a concrete large hedge to pass to the unrestricted backend.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\) denote the family produced by testing every
residual of size at most three.  Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}first\mbox{-}rank\mbox{-}boundary}\) proves that every
member is a triple contained in \(P_s\mathbin{\dot\cup}T_s\) and meeting
both parts.  Apply the parent--spouse thresholds to an optimum
\(y^{(3)}\) of the LP having only the constraints in
\(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\).  If a triple with one parent were missed, its
fractional sum would be strictly less than
\(t+2(1/2-t)=1-t<1\); if a triple with two parents were missed, its sum
would be strictly less than \(2t+(1/2-t)=1/2+t<1\).  Thus every threshold
set hits \(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\).  Integrating over uniform
\(t\in(0,1/2)\), exactly as in the proved selection-probability calculation
of Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\mbox{-}three\mbox{-}rounding}\), gives a
candidate hitting set \(A\) satisfying
\[
 c(A)\leq2\operatorname{LP}_{\leq3}
 \leq2\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c).
\]
The second inequality holds without a rank promise: every intervention that
hits the full clutter also hits its subfamily \(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\), so its
incidence vector is feasible for the restricted LP.

Alternatively, let \(A\) be an exact minimum-cost integral hitting set for
\(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\).  If the subsequent verification declares \(A\)
globally feasible, then
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}_{\leq3}\leq\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)
 \leq c(A)=\operatorname{OPT}_{\leq3},
\]
so \(A\) is globally exact.  If the rounded set is declared feasible, the
first display gives its global factor-two guarantee.  These conclusions use
verification for feasibility, not as evidence that the rank promise holds.

To perform verification, apply Lemma
\(\mathrm{lem{:}fixed\mbox{-}point\mbox{-}hedge\mbox{-}oracle}\) to
\(F_0=V\setminus A\), which contains \(s\).  A fixed point equal to
\(\{s\}\) proves that no hedge avoids \(A\), hence verification succeeds.
Otherwise the lemma returns a hedge \(F\subseteq V\setminus A\).  Minimize
it as follows.  For each \(v\in F\setminus\{s\}\), apply the same oracle to
\(F\setminus\{v\}\).  If a hedge survives, replace \(F\) by the returned
fixed-point hedge and restart.  Every replacement strictly decreases
\(|F|\), and every oracle call is polynomial, so the procedure terminates in
polynomial time.

At termination, \(F\) is inclusion-minimal.  Indeed, if a proper hedge
\(J\subsetneq F\) existed, choose
\(v\in F\setminus J\); then the survival property of the fixed-point oracle
would find a hedge in \(F\setminus\{v\}\), contradicting termination.  Thus
\(R=F\setminus\{s\}\) lies in \(\mathcal C(G,s)\).  Since
\(F\subseteq V\setminus A\), this residual is disjoint from \(A\).  But
\(A\) hit every member of \(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\); hence \(R\) cannot have
size at most three.  Therefore \(|R|>3\), which is the promised verifiable
rank-violation certificate.
